raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`--tokenizer-backend fast` only applied to a `tokenizer.json`. A `tiktoken.model` (Kimi-K3) silently stayed on tiktoken-rs, which runs at about the speed of Python tiktoken: 8 to 9 MB/s per core, so a 128k-char K3 prompt costs about 15 ms of router CPU on the TTFT path. dynamo-tokenizers 3.1.0 already ships `FastTikTokenTokenizer`, which loads the same ranks, BPE pattern and special tokens from the same `tiktoken.model`, `config.json` and `tokenizer_config.json`.

fastokens encodes exactly one input differently from the engine: U+017F (long s) directly after an apostrophe. tiktoken's `(?i:'s)` case-folds `'ſ` into the contraction and keeps ` I'ſ` as one pretoken; the fastokens scanner ends the word before the apostrophe. A sweep of every BMP codepoint through nine apostrophe and contraction contexts (571,104 inputs) against tiktoken-rs and Moonshot's `tokenization_kimi.py` found no other divergence, and the 135-case corpus below (chat, code, tool JSON, Chinese, 32k to 512k-char prompts, 60k-char base64 runs crossing the 25k split, markers typed by users) matched id for id.

## Modifications

- `adapter.rs`: for a non-json tokenizer path under `fast`, build `FastTikTokenTokenizer` and keep the tiktoken-rs tokenizer. A small wrapper routes any input whose bytes contain `C5 BF` (U+017F) to tiktoken-rs and everything else to fastokens, for both plain and segmented encodes. Load failure falls back to tiktoken-rs with a warning, as the json path does with HF.
- `stats.rs`: new `fast_tiktoken` encode backend label for the startup log.
- `REFERENCE.md`: document the tiktoken case for `--tokenizer-backend fast` and mention it in the Kimi-K3 section.
- `tests/component/tokenizer/kimi.rs`: the Kimi parity fixtures now run under both `hf` and `fast`. A second test builds a vocabulary with a merge across an apostrophe and checks that the `fast` backend matches tiktoken-rs on `'ſ` while bare fastokens does not, so the fallback can be dropped once fastokens folds the contraction.

The L1 prefix cache is unaffected: it is never built for a `.model` path (no boundary tokens are read from it), and Kimi-K3 encodes per segment anyway.

## Accuracy Tests

`cargo test -p sgl-router kimi` and `cargo test -p sgl-router --lib tokenizer::` pass; clippy with `-D warnings` is clean. On the real `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` vocabulary (revision f831ab66), the guarded fast backend produced 0 id mismatches against tiktoken-rs and the Python reference on the 135-case corpus and on the 571,104-input codepoint sweep.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Measured on an m7i.8xlarge (Xeon 8488C), Kimi-K3 vocabulary, each stack in its own process. Per-request latency pinned to one core, first encode of each input (cold caches):

| input | tiktoken-rs (before) | fast (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| short chat, ~190 chars | 35 us | ~4 us |
| medium chat, ~2k chars | 315 us | ~26 us |
| Python file, ~20k chars | 2.42 ms | ~150 us |
| 128k-char prompt | 15.4 ms | ~0.9 ms |
| 512k-char prompt | 61 ms | ~2.6 ms |

Aggregate encode throughput, all cores busy: 134 Mchars/s before, 2742 Mchars/s after (32 threads); 7.9 vs 185 Mchars/s on one core. Steady-state RSS after traffic: 69 MB before, about 340 MB after, of which the retained tiktoken-rs fallback is about 30 MB. Load time 60 ms before, about 0.8 s after.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

files.patch:
@@ -438,8 +438,11 @@ with `--locked`, so rendered bytes cannot change without a reviewed diff.
 Router tokenization sits on the TTFT path for every chat it renders. Two opt-in
 flags make it cheaper:
 
-- `--tokenizer-backend fast` encodes with fastokens (decoding stays on HF). It
-  needs a `tokenizer.json` and falls back to `hf` when fastokens cannot load it.
+- `--tokenizer-backend fast` encodes with fastokens (decoding stays on HF for a
+  `tokenizer.json`). It falls back to `hf` when fastokens cannot load a
+  `tokenizer.json`, and to `tiktoken` when it cannot load a `tiktoken.model`. On a
+  `tiktoken.model`, text containing U+017F right after an apostrophe still encodes
+  on tiktoken-rs, the one input fastokens tokenizes differently from the engine.
 - `--tokenizer-l1-cache-mb N` caches prefix tokenizations at special-token
   boundaries, so a multi-turn chat encodes only the turns added since the
   previous request. Boundaries are unconditional, non-normalized, non-stripping
@@ -598,6 +601,8 @@ through `/generate`; thinking follows the template's `enable_thinking` (on by de
 Kimi-K3 renders through `rust/sglang-processor` (dynamo-render's XTML formatter
 with SGLang's request semantics) and is tokenized with the checkpoint's chunked
 tiktoken encoding; shapes the formatter renders differently go to the worker.
+`--tokenizer-backend fast` applies to its `tiktoken.model` and encodes about 15x
+faster than the default tiktoken-rs backend.
 `--tokenizer-path` accepts a
 local `tiktoken.model` or an HF repo id, whose `tiktoken.model`, `config.json`
 and `tokenizer_config.json` are downloaded when it has no `tokenizer.json`.

@@ -1,5 +1,9 @@
 Synthetic Kimi vocabulary: the shared fixture generates 256 byte tokens, then
-adds `merges.txt` in rank order and the configured protocol markers.
+adds `merges.txt` in rank order and the configured protocol markers. Every
+multi-byte token must be reachable by merging two lower-ranked tokens (the
+intermediate merges are listed too), as fastokens refuses a vocabulary with
+unreachable tokens; special-token ids in `tokenizer_config.json` start past
+the last merge.
 `prompts.json` records token counts and SHA-256 of little-endian u32 token IDs
 from SGLang's `_encode_messages` and `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` revision
 `f831ab66814297da540d832a5235f8e904f29d06`. Regenerate in a SGLang Python environment:

@@ -1,4 +1,3 @@
-me ss ag message ro le role us er user as si st
-ant assistant sy em system to ol tool th in think res pon
-se response he ll hello wo rld world =" ca call ar gu
-ment argument js on json ty pe type ke key de cl are
+me as ss ag mess age message ro le role us er user si st assi an ant assist assistant
+sy em syst system to ol tool th in thin think re res po pon se respon response he ll hell hello
+wo rl rld world =" ca call ar gu argu nt ment argument js on json ty pe type ke key de cl are

@@ -44,6 +44,10 @@
     tokenizer = TikTokenTokenizer(model.name, **config)
 server = object.__new__(OpenAIServingChat)
 server.chat_encoding_spec = "kimi_k3"
+# A server without a reasoning parser or a custom encoding adapter, as the
+# router renders: the assistant prefix is appended with no answer opener.
+server._encoding_adapter = None
+server._reasoning_detector = None
 server.tokenizer_manager = SimpleNamespace(tokenizer=tokenizer)
 cases = json.loads((fixture / "prompts.json").read_text())
 for case in cases:
@@ -60,7 +64,9 @@
     messages = [message.model_dump() for message in request.messages]
     for message in messages:
         normalize_assistant_tool_call_arguments(message, strict=False)
-    ids = server._encode_messages(messages, request, ThinkingMode.THINKING)
+    ids = server._encode_messages(
+        messages, request, ThinkingMode.THINKING, image_data=[]
+    )
     case["token_count"] = len(ids)
     case["sha256"] = hashlib.sha256(
         b"".join(token.to_bytes(4, "little") for token in ids)
